property_summary: For any address u, getBalance(u) must return the same balance regardless of who calls it (caller-independence of the view); the mutant instead returns the caller's own balance, which differs whenever the caller is not u.

For any actor and any amounts (amt1>0, amt2), a deposit of amt1 via addToBalance can only be erased by a withdrawal that actually pays out; in the correct contract a reentrant re-deposit attempt during withdrawal reverts (guard), so the attack reverts and getBalance(actor)==amt1, while in the mutant the reentrant addToBalance succeeds and the balance ends at 0.

Whenever a withdrawal to a user succeeds, any deposit the user makes re-entrantly during the payout must not be silently erased afterwards (balance after a successful withdrawal is at least the re-entered deposit amount); the broken lock lets the re-entrant deposit through and then zeroes it, so a successful withdrawal leaves less than the re-deposited amount.

The contract's ether balance can never exceed the sum of recorded user balances (every wei accepted is credited); the broken lock lets a re-entrant deposit during a withdrawal be accepted and then silently zeroed, so address(c).balance exceeds getBalance.
